PullRequest.Title: [cherry-pick] sessions: fix workspace reselection and onboarding spotlights
PullRequest.Body:
Cherry-pick of #338335 from `main`.

## Summary

- Preserve the new-session draft when the selected workspace, provider, and Dev Container mode are unchanged. Reselecting Chat or its current host is also a no-op, while explicit workspace selections still notify onboarding.
- Revalidate spotlight targets after rendering settles. If a shown picker disappears during a workspace change, hide the spotlight and wait for its replacement using the step's existing timeout policy; skip the step if the target does not return.
- Track position-only layout shifts so the highlight and callout stay aligned with the picker, including during onboarding V2.

## Validation

- Cherry-pick applied cleanly to `release/1.140`.
- `git diff --check origin/release/1.140...HEAD` passed.
- The original PR passed `npm run compile`, 267 focused Electron unit tests, TypeScript, targeted ESLint, and whitespace checks.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The perpetual RAF semantics, synchronous geometry call, disposal lifetime, and user-paced production call path are all directly visible in repository code. Exact milliseconds vary by DOM complexity and refresh rate, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: requestAnimationFrame callbacks and synchronous DOM geometry/layout reads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One callback and getBoundingClientRect() run per display frame for the full user-controlled lifetime of every shown spotlight (about 60-144 reads/second); while the target moves, each frame also calls layout(), repeats geometry measurement, reads callout offsets, and rewrites overlay geometry.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: continuous renderer CPU/layout pressure, with increased frame time and potential UI jank/battery usage while onboarding remains open
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The overlay measured on show and only re-laid out after resize, scroll, ResizeObserver, or workbench layout events, so a stationary user-paced step did no frame-by-frame geometry work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added animate() registration creates an unconditional recursive requestAnimationFrame loop for each shown step and synchronously samples the target rectangle every frame until the step is hidden.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 197-203 newly register animate(targetWindow, ...) in show(); before this hunk, only event/observer-driven listeners scheduled layout.
Findings.Title: Stop polling spotlight geometry on every animation frame
Findings.Impact: Opening any spotlight tour or model-picker tryout now keeps the renderer sampling layout at the monitor refresh rate for as long as the user reads or interacts with the step; a one-minute pause produces roughly 3,600-8,640 geometry reads, and active picker/workbench animation additionally invokes the full overlay layout each frame.
Findings.Evidence: animate() is an unbounded recursive requestAnimationFrame helper (src/vs/base/browser/dom.ts:1766-1774). The changed callback calls target.getBoundingClientRect() every iteration; on movement it calls layout(), which reads getBoundingClientRect() again and then offsetWidth/offsetHeight after geometry writes (spotlightOverlay.ts:270-333). _showStep awaits user action with no duration bound, and production tours contain interactive workspace/model-picker steps, so the loop remains live on a realistic user-paced path.
Findings.Recommendation: Replace the perpetual poll with bounded tracking: start RAF sampling only while a relevant target/ancestor animation or a recent mutation/layout signal can move the target, stop after geometry is stable, and retain the existing resize/scroll/ResizeObserver/workbench-layout triggers for steady state.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user views an interactive onboarding spotlight or model-picker tryout, possibly leaving the step open while reading or interacting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Target resolution and one readiness frame complete before overlay.show(); thereafter the new animation-frame callback is on every rendering frame for the entire user-paced step, although it does not gate button/target input completion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible-step lifetime multiplied by display refresh rate; movement additionally scales full overlay relayout work with each animated frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one recursive requestAnimationFrame loop per visible SpotlightOverlay step; presentation runs one step at a time, so loops do not fan out, but execute at the display refresh rate until hide/disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Every frame re-reads live DOM geometry even when the rectangle is unchanged; stable values are compared but the expensive synchronous read is not avoided.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: animate() is a recursive RAF helper, the callback unconditionally calls getBoundingClientRect(), and step listeners remain registered until hide or step replacement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact layout cost depends on refresh rate, pending DOM invalidations, and workbench complexity. Production steps are user-paced and can remain visible indefinitely, so the sustained 60-144 Hz mechanism is certain even though measured frame-time impact is not available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the diff replaces event-driven steady-state positioning with continuous synchronous geometry polling and full per-frame relayout while moving.

Scenarios.Scenario: A spotlight target disappears or is replaced while rendering, animation, or an opened picker settles.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The step hides immediately, then serially resolves the replacement every 50 ms and waits for finite animations/one RAF before re-showing; replacement resolution must finish before the step can continue or skip.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one resolution attempt per 50 ms during the configured 2-10 second target timeout, plus readiness waits only when a visible target is found.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serial polling loop for the active step, bounded by the step's existing timeout policy; no parallel target probes or boundary requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; each poll resolves from an in-process provider or DOM query. The second resolution intentionally revalidates element identity after settling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the serial polling and readiness path; target replacement frequency in production is uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A target with a long finite animation can make a single readiness wait approach 600 ms, but this wait existed for the selected target before the diff and replacement retries are bounded and uncommon.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new work is bounded, serial, and required to avoid showing a stale replacement; it adds no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user reselects the current workspace, Chat option, or current quick-chat host; or selects a genuinely different workspace/provider/mode.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For a current selection, synchronous URI/provider/session-state checks now stop before async session creation and focus returns immediately. A changed selection still enters _onWorkspaceSelected -> _createNewSession -> sessionsService.openNewSession as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Asynchronous workspace-backed session creation, including the existing provider/trust/session setup behind sessionsService.openNewSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one call occurred even when the current workspace was reselected; after the diff, identical folder/provider/container-mode selections make zero calls, while changed selections still make one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every onDidSelectWorkspace event called _onWorkspaceSelected and could recreate the draft via openNewSession, including no-op reselections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For actual changed selections it remains on the selection critical path; current reselections now bypass it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One equality check per explicit picker selection; expensive creation remains one per genuinely changed selection rather than one per all selections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One handler per user selection. Existing pending workspace creation prevents reuse; the diff adds no parallelism and suppresses duplicate creation for identical selections.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No remote cache is added. Current draft/provider/container-mode state serves as the equality guard; isDevContainerEnabled is an in-memory Set lookup in the concrete provider.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event handler guard and downstream openNewSession call path are explicit, and the dev-container check is synchronous in-memory state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific session creation cost varies, but the changed behavior only removes duplicate calls and does not increase cold or warm work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: this path reduces expensive duplicate session creation and adds only constant-time in-process checks.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. One medium-severity synchronous UI regression was submitted for perpetual per-frame spotlight geometry polling; target replacement and session reselection changes are bounded or reduce prior work.
